title: Adaptive residency allocator and phased cache-heuristics for cold-start tail reduction
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets see intermittent long-tail cold starts when tenant traffic spikes or when instance churn leads to model weight eviction. Current warm pool implementations pre-load weights indiscriminately and only do coarse KV cache seeding, which increases cost and still leaves a tail risk for latency-sensitive tenants.

Goal: Implement an adaptive residency allocator that tiers model residency by predicted need and a phased cache-heuristics pipeline that seeds KV caches probabilistically to reduce observed cold-start latency while bounding extra runtime cost. This ticket covers design, prototyping, and an initial canary rollout to Dedicated fleets.

Non-goals: Full multi-tenant weighted fairness scheduler (separate epic), major changes to kernel selection logic (small hooks only).
acceptance_criteria: Measured p99 cold-start latency for canary tenants drops by >= 40% compared to baseline under synthetic spike tests
Warm pool memory overhead increases by no more than 12% for equivalent throughput compared to current warm pool baseline
Autoscaler integrates with residency allocator: nodes are not oversubscribed; 95th percentile request admission rate stays within configured throughput SLA during canary
Feature gate + runtime flag available; rollout plan tested and documented; rollback path validated
Unit and integration tests for residency decision logic, cache seeding pipeline, and admission controller added to runtime test harness
implementation_plan: Phase 1 - Design & Simulation (2 sprints): define residency tiers (resident / standby / probed / cold), residency scoring function, and cost model; run offline simulations on historical traffic traces
Phase 2 - Runtime prototype (3 weeks): implement residency allocator service + admission hooks in the orchestration layer; add kernel-aware boot ordering so frequently-used layers surface first
Phase 3 - KV phased seeder (2 weeks): implement probabilistic n-gram based KV seed with LRU-aware admission; expose seed budget per-tenant and per-fleet
Phase 4 - Autoscaler integration (2 weeks): expose residency metrics to autoscaler; add prewarm-aware scaling rule that considers in-flight preloads
Phase 5 - Canary rollout & monitoring (4 weeks): enable for 5 small/medium enterprise tenants, monitor latency, cost, and memory; iterate thresholds and budgets
Phase 6 - Gradual ramp & docs (2 weeks): broaden rollout, update runbooks, dashboard panels, and public console docs for Dedicated customers
design_tradeoffs: Eager vs. probabilistic prefetch: eager prefetch minimizes tail but can double memory/io cost; probabilistic seeding offers better cost-control but requires careful heuristics and telemetry to avoid misses

Resident slots vs. soft residency: reserving fixed slots guarantees throughput but reduces packing efficiency; soft residency with eviction scoring increases utilization but needs robust eviction fairness
Kernel-aware boot ordering introduces coupling with compilation layer; we limit scope to ordering hints rather than deep kernel changes to reduce risk
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-prefetching increases infra cost unexpectedly. Mitigation: start with strict seed budget per fleet and circuit-breaker; monitor cost delta with daily alerting.
Risk: Incorrect residency scoring favors big tenants and starves small ones. Mitigation: include tenant-weight normalization and per-tenant minimum guarantees; add fairness checks to simulator.
Risk: Autoscaler thrashes due to prewarm IO spikes. Mitigation: coordinate preload windows with autoscaler cooldown; use rate-limited background IO and admission backpressure.
metrics: p50/p95/p99 inference latency for cold-start requests
average KV cache hit rate within first 30s of instance start
warm pool memory usage delta vs baseline
cost per 1k tokens for canary tenants (to detect prefetch regressions)
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag and org-level tenant opt-in
Canary cohort: 5 tenants across 3 Dedicated fleets; enable with tight seed budgets and verbose telemetry
Day 0 smoke tests: synthetic spike replay, verify no error-rate increase, validate tail latency improvement threshold
Week 1: expand canary to 20 tenants if no regressions; adjust thresholds based on telemetry
Full fleet rollout contingent on p99 improvement and cost delta within target bounds
testing_notes: Add synthetic cold-start spike suite to perf harness (supports variable model sizes and sequence lengths)
Create unit tests for residency scoring with deterministic traces
Integration test: simulate autoscaler interaction with controlled prewarm IO to ensure no oscillation
Chaos scenario: random eviction of resident slots to ensure graceful recovery and correct KV re-seeding
